options.description: Perilaku dan Ekologi: Sosial: Mirkat sangat sosial dan hidup dalam kelompok yang disebut "geng" atau "kawan" yang terdiri dari 2 hingga 30 individu, biasanya terkait keluarga. Mereka bekerja sama dalam berburu, membesarkan anak, dan melindungi diri dari predator. Perilaku Berjaga: Salah satu perilaku mirkat yang paling terkenal adalah postur berdirinya saat berjaga. Seekor mirkat akan berdiri tegak dengan kaki belakangnya, menggunakan ekornya sebagai penyeimbang, untuk mengawasi lingkungan sekitar dari predator seperti burung pemangsa dan serigala. Mirkat yang berjaga akan mengeluarkan suara peringatan jika melihat bahaya. Makanan: Mirkat adalah omnivora, tetapi makanan utamanya adalah serangga. Mereka juga memakan laba-laba, kalajengking, reptil kecil, telur, mamalia kecil, dan terkadang tumbuhan dan buah-buahan. Reproduksi: Mirkat memiliki sistem perkembangbiakan yang kooperatif. Biasanya hanya pasangan dominan dalam kelompok yang berkembang biak, tetapi anggota kelompok lainnya membantu merawat anak-anaknya. Masa kehamilan sekitar 70 hari, dan betina dapat melahirkan hingga empat anak sekaligus. Komunikasi: Mirkat menggunakan berbagai macam vokalisasi untuk berkomunikasi satu sama lain, termasuk suara peringatan, suara panggilan, dan suara untuk interaksi sosial. Peran dalam Ekosistem: Mirkat memainkan peran penting dalam ekosistem sebagai pengendali populasi serangga dan sebagai mangsa bagi predator. Status Konservasi: Mirkat saat ini berstatus "Least Concern" (Risiko Rendah) menurut IUCN karena populasinya yang stabil dan distribusinya yang luas. Namun, hilangnya habitat dan perburuan lokal dapat menjadi ancaman bagi populasi mereka di beberapa daerah. Interaksi dengan Manusia: Mirkat sering ditampilkan di kebun binatang dan acara televisi, yang telah meningkatkan popularitasnya di seluruh dunia. Mereka juga terkadang dipelihara sebagai hewan peliharaan, meskipun ini tidak disarankan karena kebutuhan sosial dan perilaku alaminya yang kompleks.

options.description: Meerkats are small burrowing animals, living in large underground networks with multiple entrances which they leave only during the day. They are very social, living in colonies averaging 20-30 members. Animals in the same group regularly groom each other to strengthen social bonds. The alpha pair often scent-mark subordinates of the group to express their authority, and this is usually followed by the subordinates grooming the alphas and licking their faces. This behavior is also usually practiced when group members are reunited after a short period apart. Most meerkats in a group are all siblings or offspring of the alpha pair.

options.title: File:Western Lowland Gorilla in the Limbe Wildlife Center 01.jpg
options.author: OkandaLizette
options.description: Western lowland gorillas are the smallest gorillas. They are also the most widespread. They live in lush rainforests across 700,000 square kilometres (270,000 square miles) in Central Africa. Male western lowland gorillas are much larger than females, reaching an average weight of 136 kilograms (300 pounds) and an average height of 1.8 metres (6 feet). Females have an average height of 1.4 metres (4.5 feet) and weigh between 68-90 kilograms (150-200 pounds). Western gorillas are social animals and live in groups (called ‘troops’) of 2 to 30 individuals. Most groups have around five members, including a silverback male, potentially some younger blackback males, and several females, plus their infants. Gorillas spend their days and nights in nests. During the day, they find a comfortable resting spot and use foliage and branches to form a nest. Males tend to prefer the ground, while females sometimes nest in trees. Gestation in lowland gorillas lasts around nine months, and females typically reproduce every four to five years. Western lowland gorillas are what’s known as an umbrella species that indirectly protects other species around them.

options.author: Dietmar Rabich
options.description: Zebra , Kruger National Park , Mpumalanga , South Africa Planning for the national park began in the 1890s, when South African bishop Jacob Louis Grobler and other conservationists pushed for the protection of wildlife. In 1898, the area was recognized as a protected area under the administration of the South African government. In 1902/1903, the protected areas of the Kingdom of Swaziland and the region formed the first state-mandated protected area system, which eventually became Kruger National Park . In 1906, major conservation measures came into force to protect wildlife from poaching and hunting. In 1916, the Kruger National Park was formally established by the South African National Parks Act, which designated the park as a state reserve. In the 1920s, the park was opened to visitors. From 1930 onwards, the park continued to grow through the expansion of its territory.

options.description: Zebra in Makalali Game Reserve (Greater Makalali Private Game Reserve), Maruleng , Limpopo , South Africa The Makalali Game Reserve is a private game reserve in Limpopo in northeastern South Africa, west of Kruger National Park . Covering around 25,000 hectares, it features a typical lowveld savanna landscape with grasslands, bushland, and floodplains along the Makhutswi River . The reserve is a “ Big Five ” area: lions , elephants , leopards, rhinos , and buffalos live here, as do giraffes , zebras, antelopes, hyenas, and numerous bird species. In the 1990s, the area was ecologically enhanced through reintroduction projects. Makalali combines sustainable nature conservation with exclusive safari experiences. Guided game drives and bush walks allow for intensive wildlife viewing in a peaceful, natural environment.
